title: Questionnaire flow overview
purpose: Give the employee one English questionnaire with fixed steps, where each question appears only under its condition. At the end come the permit reminder and a submission that discards answers that no longer apply and makes the questionnaire read-only.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax details step (confession, spouse works, children, cross-border questions) to appear only for employees who are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to work out up front who must answer the source tax questions, and employees who are not subject are not asked for personal data no party needs
stories.priority_reason: HR's stated pain: 'I never know up front who has to answer those questions' (F-hr_transcript-b84498). Asking everyone would also break data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees subject to source tax get the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who, from the answers in the earlier steps, is subject to source tax: living abroad (whatever the nationality), or living in Switzerland without Swiss citizenship, without a C permit and not married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss citizen or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked the confession and whether they have children (with the per-child questions for each child); married employees and registered partners are also asked whether their spouse or partner works. No income type is asked: a new employee always has earned income (D-006). The tariff code is computed by Lonio from these answers, not asked (D-001).

examples.name: Non-Swiss single employee without C permit living in Switzerland
Non-Swiss married employee whose C-permit spouse lives abroad
Separated non-Swiss employee without C permit (counts as single for source tax)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees not subject to source tax skip the source tax details step
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland who holds Swiss citizenship (also with another nationality), or holds a C permit, or is married to / in a registered partnership with a Swiss citizen or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee completes the source tax status step
acceptance_criteria.then: the source tax details step is skipped entirely: no confession, children, spouse-works or cross-border questions are asked.

examples.name: Registered partner of a C-permit holder living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border questions only for residents of Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax details step reaches the cross-border questions (after the children questions)
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living in Germany are asked the German cross-border questions (daily return, then certificate of residence, reasonable return or more than 60 non-return days as they apply); employees living in Liechtenstein are asked the Liechtenstein questions (daily return, then more than 45 non-return days); employees living in Switzerland or any other country get no cross-border questions. Liechtenstein residents are asked these questions even though their result may be 'in principle no source tax liability' (D-007).

examples.name: Non-Swiss employee without C permit living in Switzerland

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through fixed steps in a set order, where every question only appears once the earlier answers show that a receiving party needs it for me
stories.so_that: I answer a short questionnaire without questions that do not apply to me
stories.priority_reason: The flow overview is a required part of the feature; asking too little blocks a registration and asking too much collects data we must not have (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Fixed order of the steps
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the steps come in this order: (1) Personal details - first name, last name, date of birth; (2) Home address - street, house number, postcode, town, country, and the canton if living in Switzerland; (3) Start - first working day; (4) Civil status - civil status and, where it applies, the spouse's or partner's date of birth; (5) Source tax status - only for employees living in Switzerland; (6) Source tax details - only for employees subject to source tax; (7) End - permit reminder where it applies, then submission. The questionnaire is in English.

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in the home address step
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is asked only if the country is Switzerland; employees living abroad are not asked for a canton (provisional, see OQ-canton-abroad).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's or partner's date of birth only for married, registered partners and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is in the civil status step
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the civil status (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership or Separated)
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked only for Married, Registered partnership and Separated; it is not asked for Single, Divorced or Widowed (see OQ-spouse-dob-other-status and OQ-civil-status-partnership).

acceptance_criteria.title: Source tax status step only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has completed the civil status step
acceptance_criteria.when: the source tax status step would start
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living abroad skip it entirely (they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality, so nationality is not asked). Employees living in Switzerland are asked their nationality ('Switzerland' for anyone holding Swiss citizenship); only non-Swiss employees are then asked whether they hold a C permit (yes or no). The permit type itself is never asked (D-005).

examples.name: Swiss citizen living in Germany (like Stefan, hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse questions only when they can change the source tax outcome
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland who is not Swiss
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered the C permit question
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's or partner's nationality is asked only if the employee has no C permit and is Married or in a Registered partnership; the spouse's C permit (yes or no) only if the spouse is not Swiss; the spouse's country of residence only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit. Separated employees are not asked these questions, as they count as single for source tax (D-003).

examples.name: Married, spouse not Swiss and without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions that no party needs are never asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is never asked for the income type or replacement income (D-006), the permit type (D-005), social insurance (AHV) data, IT equipment, a badge photo or document uploads. The insurance start date, the subject-to-source-tax result and the tariff code are derived, not asked (G-08).

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: to give each piece of information only once, even when several receiving parties need it
stories.so_that: I do not repeat myself, and HR, Pensionskasse Muster and source tax all get consistent answers from the same source
stories.priority_reason: Core goal of the feature (G-01); today HR collects spouse details by email in a slow separate round (F-hr_transcript-a45422).

acceptance_criteria.title: Each question appears once
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through all steps
acceptance_criteria.then: each piece of information is asked in exactly one step and never asked again later in the questionnaire, and every question is in English.

acceptance_criteria.title: One answer feeds every party that needs it
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer needed by more than one receiving party
acceptance_criteria.then: the same answer is recorded for every party that needs it: the country of the home address serves HR's postal address, the pension fund's canton condition and source tax; the civil status serves the pension fund's civil status and the source tax civil status group (registered partnership counts as married and separated as single for source tax, D-003); the first working day serves HR and the derived insurance start date.

examples.name: Separated non-Swiss employee: one civil status answer, two uses
Registered partner without C permit: one civil status answer, two uses
Employee living in Germany: country answer used for canton and source tax

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to end with a reminder to bring the permit on the first working day for every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on their first day
stories.priority_reason: Explicit HR wish ('half of them forget', F-hr_transcript-c53552); it saves HR follow-up but blocks no registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee reaches the end of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: employees living in Switzerland who are not Swiss citizens see the reminder; every employee living abroad sees it, whatever their nationality (nationality is not asked of them); Swiss citizens living in Switzerland do not see it.

examples.name: Swiss citizen living in Germany (like Stefan, hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: The reminder collects no data and is worded by HR
acceptance_criteria.then: it only reminds the employee to bring their permit on the first working day; it asks nothing and records no answer. HR provides the wording, so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see that it does not apply to them. No extra 'Swiss citizen' question is added just for the reminder.

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: to change earlier answers without losing my input while I go back and forth, and to have answers to questions that no longer apply dropped when I submit
stories.so_that: I can correct myself easily, and no personal data that no receiving party needs is kept about me
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a hard constraint: collecting data we must not have is a stated risk (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are kept while the employee goes back and forth
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered a question and then changes an earlier answer so that the question no longer applies
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes the earlier answer back before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: the question applies again and the previously given answer is still there; no input is lost.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers to questions that no longer apply are discarded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answers to questions that no longer apply after a change of an earlier answer
acceptance_criteria.then: only answers to questions that apply to the submitted answers are recorded; all other answers are discarded and not recorded for any party.

examples.name: Employee first entered Switzerland and an Italian nationality, then changed the country to Germany
Employee first chose Married and gave a spouse's date of birth, then changed to Single
Non-Swiss employee first answered no C permit and the source tax details, then changed to yes

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to become read-only for the employee once submitted, and every derived result to be derived again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: later changes go through HR, and derived values such as the insurance start date never go stale at the receiving parties
stories.priority_reason: A missed update after Julia's first working day moved caused a wrong date at the pension fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66).

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee cannot change answers after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can see the answers but cannot change them. Later changes (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) are made by HR; how HR does this is part of the later HR-side spec (D-034).

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer recorded for an employee is changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax, and the tariff code are all derived again from the latest answers. For the first working day only the latest date counts; no history of earlier dates is kept.

examples.name: Nationality corrected to Switzerland after submission
Non-Swiss employee without C permit marries a Swiss citizen living in Switzerland after submission
Swiss citizen moves from Switzerland to Germany after submission
